subject: research/swe-errlabel
professional: a senior content-analysis / annotation methodologist (the kind who reviews coding-scheme validation for Communication Methods and Measures or an MSR/ICSE empirical track). They would check first whether the codebook was fixed before labelling, whether there is a second independent coder and an inter-coder kappa with an interval, whether the headline category ('ci-or-tooling') is well defined enough that two coders agree on it, and whether the diagnosis of why the rules miss it is right

evidence.correctness: Every reported number recomputes with tools the author did not use. Rerun `cd research/swe-errlabel && python3 experiments/run.py` is byte-identical to experiments/results.txt; `python3 experiments/sample.py` is byte-identical to data/to_label.tsv (222 entries, seed 20261018); figure.py regenerates precision_recall.svg identically. Independent script indep.py (scikit-learn + statsmodels, its own regex application, its own redraw of the seeded sample): accuracy 40/60 = 0.6667, statsmodels Wilson (0.5406, 0.7727) = README 54.1% to 77.3%; sklearn cohen_kappa_score 0.5862 = 0.59; sklearn confusion_matrix equals the results.txt matrix cell for cell; precision/recall 0.556/1.0, 0.857/1.0, 0.923/0.923, n/a/0, 0.706/0.545, 0.357/1.0 = README; the 222-entry population counts (environment 62, unclassified 54, own-mistake 47, collision 38, timeout 15, ci-or-tooling 6) equal swe-errors' results.txt. Not 4: the hand labels are the measurement and rest on one non-independent coder; my own (non-blind) second reading agrees with them at kappa 0.87 but moves 6 entries, 5 of them out of ci-or-tooling, under a defensible tie-break.
evidence.completeness: README promises: tests (5 OK in 0.004 s), sample.py reproduces the committed blind sample (byte-identical), run.py reproduces results.txt (byte-identical), figure.py reproduces the SVG (identical), every disagreement listed with its text (20 rows present), live page https://marisstella.app/research/swe-errlabel/ (HTTP 200, title 'Do the swe-errors keyword rules sort...', figure served at /research/swe-errlabel/precision_recall.svg 200 image/svg+xml). Everything claimed as done is present and runs end to end. The second labeller, held-out rule fix and swe-orgs check are honestly listed as Next steps, not done.
evidence.verification: `cd research/swe-errlabel && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: Ran 5 tests in 0.004s OK (plus ResourceWarning for unclosed files from read_tsv). Five non-equivalent mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (confusion transposed, Wilson n*n -> n, kappa denominator 1-pe -> 1+pe), 2 survived: cohen_kappa's expected agreement using the hand marginals twice (__init__.py:44, a Scott's-pi-style change; the only chance test has a degenerate setup where both give 0) and run.py:23 computing precision as tp/hand (swaps precision and recall in results.txt and the figure; run.py has no test and nothing pins results.txt). No test checks the headline 40/60 or kappa 0.59 against the committed data.
evidence.craft: Read src/swe_errlabel/__init__.py (56 lines), tests/test_errlabel.py, experiments/run.py, sample.py, figure.py. Stdlib only, small pure functions, sample and figure scripted rather than hand-typed, figure parsed from results.txt. Defects: read_tsv opens files without closing (ResourceWarning in the test run, __init__.py:14); the package mutates sys.path at import to reach the sibling swe-errors source (__init__.py:7), so it is not installable as the pyproject claims; precision/recall division lives untested in run.py rather than in per_class; confusion() raises KeyError on an unknown label with no message.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 40/60, Wilson interval, kappa, confusion, per-class numbers and the seven own-mistake -> unclassified entries are all in results.txt and recompute. Three claims are wrong or misstated: (1) README:8 explains that ci-or-tooling never wins because 'earlier rules in the ordered list (collision, environment, own-mistake) match first, or no keyword fires'; own-mistake is AFTER ci-or-tooling in swe-errors' RULES, environment matches none of the nine, and by direct regex test 8 of 9 hand-labelled ci entries contain no ci-or-tooling keyword at all; only 957.0 is lost to rule order. (2) README:8 'So swe-errors reports no such category': swe-errors/experiments/results.txt reports ci-or-tooling 6 entries (2.7%) on the full 222. (3) README:10 says the three ci entries read as collisions 'mention a conflict or stale check'; the matching words are 'sibling' (651.0, 957.0) and 'conflict' (976.0), none 'stale'. research/README.md:666 calls the sample 'blind hand-labelled' while README:31 says the labeller had read the keyword lists. Limitations section is otherwise candid and specific.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wanting to know whether swe-errors' category shares can be trusted, or to build a better classifier. The committed sample, labels and disagreement list make the check reproducible and extensible, which is useful. But the actionable conclusion is weak: the proposed fix (Next steps, README:39, 'ordering ci-or-tooling before collision') would recover 1 of the 9 missed entries, because the miss is vocabulary, not order; and the ci-or-tooling class itself is codebook-dependent (5 of its 9 entries are a repository check correctly catching the run's own change, which a second coder can as defensibly call own-mistake: under that reading the class has 3 entries and rule agreement is 45/60 = 75%, kappa 0.68). Nearest prior work: validation of automatic/recorded labels against manual coding in SE (Herzig, Just & Zeller, ICSE 2013, 'It's not a bug, it's a feature': 33.8% of issue reports misclassified), dictionary-method validation in text-as-data (Grimmer & Stewart 2013, 'validate, validate, validate'), and LLM-agent failure taxonomies with multi-annotator kappa (Cemri et al. 2025, MAST, kappa 0.88). None is cited. The result is new only as an internal measurement of this repository's own rules; its arithmetic is sound, its mechanism explanation is not. Not part of any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md and well short of the PhD bar.
evidence.domain: Against standard content-analysis practice (Krippendorff 2018; Landis & Koch 1977 for interpreting kappa): a single, non-independent coder (disclosed); no evidence the codebook was fixed before labelling beyond the README's say-so; kappa reported with no interval (my percentile bootstrap, 5000 reps: 0.44 to 0.72, spanning 'moderate' to 'substantial'); the 'moderate' reading uses Landis & Koch's bands without citing them; the ci-or-tooling definition ('a repository check ... failing or misbehaving') does not separate a check that correctly caught the run's change from a check that malfunctioned, and that ambiguity drives the headline finding. Paired entries from the same run treated as independent (disclosed). A methodologist would accept the computation and reject the headline as stated.

defects.what: Wrong diagnosis of the headline finding: README says ci-or-tooling never wins because earlier rules (collision, environment, own-mistake) match first; own-mistake is a later rule, environment matches none, and 8 of 9 hand-labelled ci entries contain no ci-or-tooling keyword. Only 957.0 is lost to order, so the Next-steps fix (README:39, reorder ci-or-tooling before collision) would recover 1 of 9
'So swe-errors reports no such category' is false: swe-errors' results.txt reports ci-or-tooling at 6 entries (2.7%) of 222; it never wins in this 60-entry sample only

The ci-or-tooling class definition does not separate a repository check that correctly caught the run's own change (541.0, 590.0, 590.1, 651.0, 222.1) from tooling that malfunctioned; under a defensible alternative tie-break the class shrinks from 9 to 3 and rule agreement rises from 66.7% to 75% (kappa 0.59 -> 0.68). The headline finding rests on this single non-independent coder's convention, and kappa is reported without an interval (bootstrap 0.44 to 0.72)

Tests do not pin results: no test checks 40/60 or kappa against the committed data; cohen_kappa's expected-agreement marginal can be swapped (Scott's pi style) and run.py's precision can be computed as tp/hand, both with all tests green

Nearest prior work on validating automatic/recorded labels against manual coding is not cited (Herzig, Just & Zeller ICSE 2013; Grimmer & Stewart 2013; Cemri et al. 2025 MAST agent-failure taxonomy), nor Landis & Koch (1977) for the 'moderate' reading of kappa
README says the three ci entries read as collisions 'mention a conflict or stale check'; the matching words are 'sibling' (twice) and 'conflict', none 'stale'
research index calls the sample 'blind hand-labelled' while the project README says the labeller had read the keyword lists (blind only to the rules' output)
read_tsv leaves files open (ResourceWarning in every test run) and the package inserts the sibling swe-errors src into sys.path at import, so it is not installable on its own despite pyproject.toml

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible validation note whose arithmetic is right and whose headline explanation is not. Every number recomputes with scikit-learn and statsmodels (40/60, Wilson 54.1-77.3%, kappa 0.586, the full confusion matrix and per-class precision/recall), the seeded sample redraws to the same 60 ids, and run.py, sample.py and figure.py reproduce their committed outputs byte for byte. It misses the bar on claims and verification: the README attributes the ci-or-tooling miss to rule order when 8 of 9 such entries have no ci keyword at all (so its proposed reorder fixes 1 of 9), says swe-errors reports no such category when it reports 6 entries (2.7%), and 2 of 5 seeded mutants survive because nothing pins the committed results. The ci-or-tooling class is itself codebook-fragile: a second (non-blind) reading moves 5 of its 9 entries to own-mistake and lifts agreement to 75%. One non-independent coder, no kappa interval and no cited prior work keep it well short of the research bar.
